label: late original-phase position (t>=6), token-weighted
explanation: Fires only while the original tokens are being read, and only at late absolute positions: never at t<=2, almost never at t=3-4, and the rate climbs with position (13% at t=5, 41% at t=6, 65% at t=7, 74% at t=8). That is why it is concentrated in long sequences (L=8-9) on the last 1-3 tokens before <DEL>. It never fires on the <DEL> step or anywhere in the copy phase. Within late positions the input token changes the firing rate: i, v, m, l, h, 3, b, 2, z, d, u and 0 fire most often, while a, o, n, k, t, y, f, e, p, r and c often stay silent. First occurrences of a token, and sequences with more digits, fire somewhat more often. The plain position rule (phase==0 & t>=6) gets dev F1 0.66 with mass recall 0.92. Adding the token set lifts dev F1 to 0.73 (precision 0.70, recall 0.76, mass recall 0.87). Most of the remaining errors are token-dependent silences at t>=6 and weak activations at t=5.
